purpose: A VDMOS .model card's m is the body diode's grading coefficient (ngspice vdmos.c:121), never the multiplier, and the body diode with RB sits on the external source and drain (vdmosset.c:378-398, vdmosload.c:723-724, 888). ESPice bound the card's m=0.548 to the multiplicity (2.3471 mA forward, 0.548 IS reverse) and put the diode behind RS and RD.

oracle.derivation: ngspice 44.2 batch run of this deck, values read from its ASCII raw. Corroborated by the closed forms (Vt = kT/q at 300.15 K): D1 and MF are one Shockley junction, N = 1.564, with 3.8 mOhm in series, 4.96707 mA at 0.5 V; D2 and MR at -2 V carry dioload.c's reverse branch -IS(1 - (3 N Vt/(2e))^3) - 2 V GMIN = -2.13018e-8 A; the 1 kHz reverse admittance is j 2 pi 1k CJO/(1 + 2/VJ)^0.548 = j 3.79100e-6 S, where a grading left at 0.5 gives j 4.38753e-6 S.
oracle.tolerance: rtol 1e-3, ngspice's reltol: every terminal is pinned, and ESPice matched each column to 4e-6 or better once the card's m bound the grading and the diode left RS and RD (measured with mj= and RS=RD=0 on the old build). The reverse 1 kHz point keeps 7.1e-10 S of ngspice's real part that ESPice does not: vdmosload.c:797 takes gdb = IS*3*arg/vd with arg not cubed, where dioload.c cubes it; that is 1.9e-4 of the admittance, inside rtol. atol 1e-12 A.
